subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs to open models
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightcommerce.com>
Cc: Aisha Gupta <aisha@brightcommerce.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs to open models

Samir / Aisha —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side to make sure we captured the pain, goals, and next steps correctly. If I've missed anything, reply with corrections.

Pain points you shared:
- Heavy monthly spend on current OpenAI/Anthropic usage with unpredictable token costs.
- Latency spikes during peak checkout flows causing customer frustration.
- Concerns about vendor lock-in and future pricing/availability risk.

Current stack / how you're using LLMs:
- OpenAI for chat generation (GPT-4 family) — session-based chat for customer support and product recommendations.
- Anthropic for a few safety-critical moderation pipelines.
- Mix of synchronous API calls and an event-driven batch enrichment pipeline.

Success criteria for migration (your priorities):
1) Cost predictability / reduce per-token spend by at least 40% for the recommendation workload.
2) Maintain or improve 95th percentile latency for customer-facing chat flows.
3) Compatibility with existing OpenAI/Anthropic prompts + minimal code changes (SDK/endpoint parity or adapter layer).
4) Maintain current safety/moderation posture — SOC2 evidence and auditability required.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial):
- Llama 2 family (fine-tune / adapter friendly)
- Mistral Large / Mix (strong instruction-following at lower cost)
- Falcon 40B (good throughput on GPU + quantization)
- Hugging Face/OpenAssistant variants for specialized safety models

Compatibility needs / constraints:
- Need an API adapter layer that mimics OpenAI/Anthropic request/response shapes (few changes to product code).
- Tokenization/temperature/stop-sequence parity is important for recommendation scoring.
- Expectation of a staged rollout (test environment -> canary -> full prod) with rollback.

Next steps we agreed on:
- I will send a compatibility worksheet (attached) for your eng team to fill in — helps prioritize which endpoints need exact parity. (attached: redwood-compat-worksheet.xlsx)
- We'll scope a 6-week POC focused on the recommendation pipeline: baseline perf/cost, model comparison, and a safety/regression check.
- Provide an initial starter quote and a recommended PoC plan — attaching a high-level pricing proposal. (attached: redwood-pricing-proposal.pdf)
- Rishi and Aditya (internal) will join the technical deep-dive next week to discuss inference runtime, batching, and quantization options.

Action items for BrightCommerce:
- Fill out the compatibility worksheet by Tue 16 Jun.
- Share a sample of typical request/response sizes and a rough monthly token estimate for the recommendation and chat workloads.

If that looks good, let's lock a 60-minute technical deep-dive the week of Jun 22. I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks again — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0143
Redwood Inference — production-grade LLM inference

Attachments: redwood-compat-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), redwood-pricing-proposal.pdf (proposal stub)

From: Samir Patel <samir@brightcommerce.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aisha Gupta <aisha@brightcommerce.com>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs to open models

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap, this captures it well. A few clarifications from our side:

- On throughput: recommendation pipeline sees peak bursts up to ~1,800 reqs/min during promotions, baseline ~350 reqs/min. Latency SLO we care about is <= 300ms P95 for chat calls.
- For security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II and data residency in US-only for PII-containing logs. We'll need an evidence bundle and a CSO call during the POC.
- For compatibility worksheet: we'll aim to complete it by Tue 16 Jun — sending to our infra lead.

Two asks from our eng lead: 
1) Can you share a short note on tokenization differences we might run into (OpenAI vs Llama/Mistral) and any adapter best-practices?
2) What's the expected infra footprint for the recommendation model during POC (gpus / pods estimate)?

Happy to lock the deep-dive on Jun 23 or 24 — mornings PDT work best.

—
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Engineering | BrightCommerce
samir@brightcommerce.com | (212) 555-0108

Attachments referenced: SOC2_RFI_stub.pdf (we'll send our RFI formally later)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightcommerce.com>
Cc: Aisha Gupta <aisha@brightcommerce.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs to open models

Samir —

Appreciate the fast follow. Quick answers to the two asks and next steps: 

Tokenization / adapter note (short):
- Primary gap is tokenizer differences (byte-pair vs unigram variations) that can slightly shift token counts and stop-sequence behavior.
- Best practice: add a lightweight adapter layer that canonicalizes requests (normalize whitespace, enforce stop sequences server-side) and reports token counts from the chosen model's tokenizer so you can compare apples-to-apples.
- For prompt parity, test with a 1k-sample set of prompts and measure generation divergence; we can help run that as part of the POC.

Expected infra footprint (POC estimate for recommendation workload):
- 2 x A100-80GB (quantized model + batchable runtime) should cover your peak for initial experiments with good headroom — we can adjust with dynamic batching.
- If you prefer lower-cost instances, we can try 4 x A10G with more aggressive quantization; we'll benchmark both during week 1 of the POC.

Compliance / SOC2: we'll share our SOC2 Type II report and a short evidence bundle for the POC. I'll loop our compliance contact and send a link once we confirm the NDA/POC scope.

Proposed mutual action plan (high level):
- Week 0: compatibility worksheet + sample payloads (BrightCommerce)
- Week 1: infra sizing + baseline cost/latency measurement on a small sample set (Redwood + BrightCommerce)
- Weeks 2-4: model experiments (Llama2 / Mistral / Falcon), safety/regression checks; choose finalist
- Weeks 5-6: canary rollout on recommendation pipeline + production smoke tests; handoff docs

I'll attach a short starter pricing proposal (same file I sent earlier) and a sample statement of work outline.

Can we aim to schedule 60m on Tue Jun 23 10:00am PDT? I'll send a calendar invite and include Rishi/Aditya for the technical portion.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0143

Attachments: redwood-pricing-proposal.pdf, SOC2_RFI_stub.pdf (stub)
